summary: Phase 3 — Razorpay refill for AI-credits wallet. Backend: 16/16 pytest cases PASS (100%) covering GET /api/ai-wallet/packs (3 packs, INR pricing, fx_source live/cache/fallback, markup_pct 10% user / 1% admin, min_custom_credits=150), POST /api/ai-wallet/refill/quote (full breakdown, below_min=false at 1000 credits, 400 at 10 credits, pack_id='pro' works, invalid pack_id → 400, cost_inr+markup_inr≈total_inr, total_paise=total_inr*100), POST /api/ai-wallet/refill/order (returns order_id starting with 'order_', amount in paise, key_id, route_applied bool, ai_wallet_orders doc persisted), POST /api/ai-wallet/refill/verify (bogus signature → 400, missing fields → 400), GET /api/ai-wallet/refill/checkout (text/html containing checkout.razorpay.com + order_id + amount), PUT /api/admin/ai-wallet/config gating (regular user 403, plain admin 403, super_admin 200 + packs reflect updated markup), super_admin can update credit_packs + route_linked_account_id + min_custom_credits + blended_usd_per_mtok + usd_to_inr_fallback. NOTE: against this account Razorpay Route is NOT activated for acc_SyPciERWCkmA6R so route_applied returns false — graceful fallback path executes correctly (order is still created). Live FX returned 95.22 (cache), so user-facing prices on this run were ₹104.74/₹418.98/₹1047.45 (10% markup) and admin-facing ₹96.18/₹384.70/₹961.75 (1% markup); spec's ~₹99/₹396/₹990 estimate assumed the ₹90 fallback. Frontend (admin@test.com, mobile 390x844): /ai-wallet renders correctly — balance card (200.00), 3 pack cards Starter/Pro/Power with ₹ buttons and badges (Starter/Popular/Best value), 'Custom amount' input with 'Get price' button working (1000 credits → ₹19.24 with 'Gemini cost ₹19.04 + 1% fee ₹0.19' breakdown shown), 'Grant credits' admin section visible. The super-admin-only Default starting balances / Refill pricing / Markup / FX / Route inputs are present in ai-wallet.tsx (lines 292-373) but could NOT be exercised via UI because the documented super_admin (veales.vedic.decisions@gmail.com) is blocked behind the WhatsApp OTP gate (same constraint flagged in iteration_64). The backend tests fully validate that flow end-to-end including config persistence and packs reflecting updated markup.

INFO: Backend regression file /app/backend/tests/test_iter65_ai_wallet_refill.py is the canonical Phase-3 test suite (16 cases). Reuses module-scoped fixture that resets config to spec defaults and restores markup_user_pct=10 at teardown.

INFO: ai_wallet_orders documents are created with `amount_paise`, `breakdown`, `route_applied`, `fx_source`, `status='created'` — verified persisting; status flips to 'paid' only on successful /verify (HMAC signature match).
critical_code_review_comments: core/ai_billing.price_for_credits is deterministic and matches the spec: cost_usd = credits*tpc*blended/1e6, total_usd = cost_usd*(1+markup/100), then *fx. Verified numerically: 1000 credits @ 100 tpc @ $2/Mtok @ 1.10 markup @ fx≈95.22 ⇒ ₹20.95 (cost ₹19.04 + markup ₹1.90); rounding-safe via paise integer math.

Route fallback (routes/ai_wallet.py:209-224): if transfers payload fails (Route not enabled), code retries the same order WITHOUT transfers and sets route_applied=false. Order still created — confirmed live behaviour on this account.

Verify endpoint computes HMAC-SHA256 over '{order_id}|{payment_id}' using key_secret — standard Razorpay handshake. Confirmed 400 on bogus signature. Idempotency: re-posting the same valid signature after status='paid' returns {message:'Payment already processed', credits_added:0} — code path is correct (lines 268-270).

Frontend ai-wallet.tsx uses BASE_URL = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL || process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL — correct env-var usage. WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(checkout URL) is mobile-safe.
Admin role (admin@test.com) correctly does NOT see the Super-Admin config card (gated by `isSuperAdmin = role === 'super_admin'`). Verified.

rca_of_issue: No bug. The only nuance is route_applied=false on this account — that is by design (graceful fallback when Razorpay Route is not enabled on the linked account); orders are still created and checkout still works, the markup just stays in the primary account instead of being split. This matches the explicit spec: 'with graceful fallback if Route not enabled'.
